blocks.heading: It started with the switch from 4G to Wi-Fi.
blocks.left: On 4G, customers could be identified automatically. After switching to Wi-Fi, they were unexpectedly asked for a password without understanding why.
blocks.right: Instead of fixing only that moment, we used it to uplift the wider login experience—clearer guidance, faster returning access, biometrics, account handling, and secure fallbacks. I led the one-month project as the sole designer, working with product owners and the testing team.

blocks.heading: From an unexplained interruption to a guided login journey.

blocks.heading: The journey was familiar. The rules changed with the network.
blocks.left: On 4G, the app could identify the customer's number automatically. We also needed to reassure them that using the app would not consume their mobile data.
blocks.right: When customers switched to Wi-Fi, that automatic detection was no longer available. The experience had to explain the change clearly and guide them to enter their password.

blocks.heading: Returning should feel effortless.
blocks.body: Biometrics gave returning customers a faster way in, while the updated journey kept the right account and login choices visible when they were needed.

blocks.heading: A cancelled prompt should not end the journey.
blocks.body: If biometrics were cancelled or unavailable, customers could continue with another secure login method instead of feeling stuck.

blocks.heading: We tested two moments for password creation.
blocks.body: Variant A asked customers to create a password during registration. Variant B moved password creation until after registration. The goal was to learn which moment could reduce drop-off and prevent customers from abandoning the app. The final experiment result was still being evaluated.

blocks.quote: A clearer login journey, delivered in one month.
blocks.body: The revamp clarified what happens when customers move from 4G to Wi-Fi, made returning access faster, and introduced fallbacks that kept people moving.
